- Familiarity with relational databases and writing SQL queries (e.g., PostgreSQL).

- Excellent problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn new enterprise technologies and methodologies.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.

- Hands-on project experience with frontend frameworks, specifically React

- Exposure to cloud computing environments and services, particularly AWS.

- Familiarity with modern data warehousing concepts and ELT/ETL tools (e.g., Redshift, Airbyte).

Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for.

Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world.

We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads.

What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life.

We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies.

ERPs ran the physical world for half a century. Dryft is building the intelligence layer that will power the next.

​

THE ROLE

As a Member of Technical Staff Intern, you'll build the system that decides how some of the largest manufacturers in the world operate. That means combining agent-based reasoning with mathematical optimization and simulation on large-scale industrial data.

- Build agents people trust – when an agent runs a factory's week, the largest industrial companies in the world have to trust it with their critical processes and understand every decision it makes; you build the routing, orchestration and guardrails behind that

- Ship features end-to-end – you understand the user need, and you get the freedom to build it across the LLM pipeline, infrastructure, backend and frontend, in production in your first weeks

- Work close to the users – sit with the planners who use it, see what would make their work 10x faster, and build it

You'll own your own features from day one, and what you ship decides what a plant does next week.

​

YOU

- Full-stack shipper – you've shipped production code end-to-end, you build scalable backend and infra that handles massive amounts of structured and unstructured data, and you build the interface that makes it usable

- Highly technical – you've built something technically hard, and you can walk us through every decision behind it

- Product sense – you spot the feature hiding in a user's complaint, and you've deleted your own favorite one because nobody used it

- You care about getting it right – you know when it has to be 100% and when to keep it simple, and when it matters, you're still chasing the root cause at 2am

- Sense of urgency – you'd rather ship it tonight than sleep on an open PR

- Relocation – you're ready to work onsite in San Francisco (we support visa)

​

TECH STACK

- FE (TypeScript): React, Chakra UI v3, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, Vite

- BE (Python): FastAPI with Pydantic v2, Temporal, Postgres with pgvector, dagster

- AI: Pydantic AI, Langfuse

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.

Role Overview

Right now, Quality and Manufacturing at our Vineyard facility each keep their own calibration records for the measuring tools used to build and certify Seagliders. Tools could be used past their calibration due date without anyone catching it, and the measurement evidence behind our certification work is weaker than it should be. As we ramp up build volume next year, untangling divergent systems only gets harder, which is exactly why we want to get this right now, while the problem is still solvable from the ground up.

As our Quality Intern, you'll take full ownership of designing and building that solution. You'll dig into engineering drawings to understand what level of precision each tool actually needs to protect, merge mismatched sets of records into a single trustworthy register and due-date schedule in ION, and spend real time on the shop floor talking with technicians to understand how tools are actually tracked and used day to day; this is critical. You'll be joining the Manufacturing & Supply Chain team at a moment when the systems you help build will directly shape how reliably we can scale production. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by turning scattered, high-stakes information into something clean, trustworthy, and lasting — and who wants real ownership of a project from first audit to final presentation — we'd love to have you on the team.

What You'll Do

- Audit the Current State: You'll track down and catalog every measuring tool in use across Quality and Manufacturing, building a clear picture of what exists today and where the two teams' records diverge.

- Build the Unified Register: You'll merge two previously disconnected sets of calibration records into a single, standardized register in ION that both teams can rely on and maintain going forward.

- Define the Due-Date Schedule: Using engineering drawings and tolerance requirements, you'll determine which tools need calibrating, how often, and build the schedule that keeps everyone ahead of due dates.

- Get Hands-On With Technicians: You'll spend real time on the shop floor, talking directly with Quality and Manufacturing staff to understand how tools are actually used and tracked, not just how the paperwork says they should be.

- Catch What the Spreadsheets Miss: You'll dig into mismatched IDs, conflicting intervals, and missing due dates, making judgment calls about what belongs in the final system.

- Align Two Teams on One Process: You'll work with both Quality and Manufacturing to get everyone bought into a single shared process, rather than two teams quietly working around each other.

- Present Your Finished System: At the end of your term, you'll present the completed calibration register and schedule directly to Quality and Manufacturing leadership, along with documentation the team will keep using after you're gone.

What You'll Bring

- Comfort With Engineering Drawings: You can read a drawing and understand tolerances well enough to reason about which tools need calibration and how tightly — not just copy an existing list.

- Sharp Spreadsheet Skills: You're accurate and efficient working across large sets of data, since merging two record systems and catching inconsistencies is fundamentally spreadsheet work.

- Meticulous Attention to Records: You understand that a wrong serial number or due date isn't a small mistake — it's the difference between a tool being trustworthy and a tool being used out of calibration unnoticed.

- Ease on the Shop Floor: You're comfortable walking up to technicians, asking questions, and helping two groups find common ground on how something should actually work.

- Hands-On Tool Experience: Any direct experience with measuring tools helps you recognize tool types quickly and understand what calibration is really protecting.

- Familiarity With Quality Standards: Exposure to ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 17025 gives you a useful head start on what a compliant register needs to capture, like traceability and intervals.

- Basic Scripting a Plus: Some Python or SQL could help you automate comparisons between the two tool lists, though spreadsheets can get the job done too.

Who We're Looking For

- Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

- Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.
